# Roster

> Roster is an agent that runs performance reviews for your AI coding agents, and tests whether its call holds.

## The result

Four AI coding setups built this repo. Roster reviewed them and replaced Claude Code + Sonnet 5.5 (**B**) with Claude Code on DeepSeek Flash (**E**). Before it made that call, we froze 40 new build tasks and their acceptance tests (hash published). Then every task was built twice, by B and by E, and graded blind.

| Forward test, pre-registered (interim: 26 valid pairs) | |
|---|---|
| Tasks only E passed | **6** |
| Tasks only B passed | **0** |
| Both passed / both failed | 17 / 3 |
| McNemar exact, two-sided | **p = 0.031** |
| Cost per task | E cheaper in 26 of 26 pairs: median $0.023 vs $0.155 (Wilcoxon p < 0.001) |

Every number here comes from [`docs/FACTS.md`](docs/FACTS.md) or [`reports/self/forward.json`](reports/self/forward.json), both generated from the run. The pairs are on the [experiment page](https://roster-five-chi.vercel.app/experiment).

**How the call was made: v1, then v2.**
- **v1:** Roster's first review promoted E on a 0–0 tie. Every setup failed all 10 replayed tasks with hidden tests, so the cheaper one won, with no quality signal. We disclosed that before the forward run ([amendment 7](experiments/PREREGISTRATION.md)).
- **v2:** we fixed the replay and taught the gate to refuse a tie with no signal.
- **Review 1b:** the same 10 tasks under v2. B passes 1, E passes 0, and the gate **rejects** E.
- **What that means:** replaying past tasks is a weak signal. The pre-registered forward test is the strong one, and it says the call held.

## What it does

It reads every session your coding agents recorded with [Entire](https://entire.io), and for each one works out:
- what it cost
- whether its change survived
- whether it was reverted, or reworked by a person

Then it tests a better setup on your own past tasks, and ships that setup only if nothing regresses.

**Live:**
- [roster-five-chi.vercel.app](https://roster-five-chi.vercel.app)
- [our own AI team's review](https://roster-five-chi.vercel.app/r/rajkaria/roster)
- [all reviews](https://roster-five-chi.vercel.app/r)

## Architecture

- **Agent and CLI:** TypeScript on Bun (`bun:sqlite`, `bun test`).
- **Coordinator:** a tool-calling loop on DeepSeek's OpenAI-compatible API (`src/llm`). See §"Models Roster itself uses".
- **Web:** Next.js in `web/`, with its own `package.json`. The prebuild step copies `reports/` into `web/public/data`.
- **Sandboxes:** local temp dirs for this repo; microVMs for public repos.

### Layout

```
src/types.ts                         shared contracts
src/ingest/ src/identity/ src/price/
src/score/ src/difficulty/ src/review/
src/sandbox/ src/replay/ src/harness/{claude,codex}.ts src/grade/ src/gate/
src/agent/ src/candidates/ src/obs/ src/cfo/ src/act/ src/forward/
src/cli.ts + src/cli/<cmd>.ts
scripts/ (run-setup.sh, ledger.ts, sumcheck.ts, facts.ts, corpus-find.ts)
reports/ (generated JSON)   docs/FACTS.md (generated)   experiments/   setups/   web/   tests/
```

### CLI

```
roster review <repo> [--observational] [--budget <usd>] [--out reports/<slug>]
roster replay <repo> --tasks plan.json
roster gate <repo>
roster act <repo> [--pr]
roster book [--org <org>]
roster forward --backlog experiments/forward-backlog.md --pair OLD,NEW --parallel 4
roster acceptance --backlog experiments/forward-backlog.md --out experiments/acceptance/
roster facts
```

### Data model (`.roster/roster.db`, exported to `reports/*.json`)
- **`sessions`:**
  - `id, repo, checkpoint_id, harness, model, rules_hash, setup_id`
  - `tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write, cost_usd, n_user_prompts`
  - `first_prompt, commit_sha, started_at, ended_at, files[], entire_url, source`
- **`outcomes`:** `session_id, status (mature|too_young), survival, reverted, rework_human, rework_agent, unattended, tests_at_commit, difficulty, tercile`
- **`setups`:** `id, harness, model, rules_hash, rules_path, label`
- **`plans`:** `id, review_id, json, rationale, created_at`
- **`replays`:**
  - `id, plan_id, task_session_id, setup_id, attempt, isolation_proof, turns, duration_ms, cost_usd`
  - `hidden_pass, suite_pass, scope_ok, judge_equiv, failure_codes[], verdict, transcript_ref, trace_url`
- **`gate_decisions`:** `id, plan_id, candidate, verdict, reasons[], trace_url`
- **`forward_pairs`:** `task_id, setup_old, setup_new, pass_old, pass_new, cost_old, cost_new, merged, blind_labels, seed`
- **`events`:** an append-only step log. Every step is idempotent, and runs resume from here.

# Pre-registration: Roster's self-build experiment

**Registered:** 2026-10-10, during neatHack. The registration is the commit that first adds this file. Later changes go only in **Amendments** at the bottom, dated, and nothing above that heading is edited.

## The question
Four coding-agent setups (`setups/A.json`–`D.json`) build this repository. Partway through the build, Roster reviews their recorded sessions:
1. It names a suspect setup.
2. It replays the suspect's real past tasks under candidate setups.
3. It promotes a candidate only if nothing regresses.

We test whether that decision holds on new work that didn't exist when the decision was made.

- **H1 (primary):** on the forward backlog, the setup Roster promotes passes more tasks than the setup it demotes.
  - Test: McNemar exact over paired tasks, two-sided, α = 0.05.
- **H2 (secondary):** the promoted setup's cost per task is no higher than the demoted setup's.
  - Test: Wilcoxon signed-rank over the paired costs.

## Design
- **Build tasks before the review:**
  - Each task has an id `Txx`.
